description: Decision-scenario regression evals; assertions check decisions, not wording. Run against any rewrite of SKILL.md before merging it, and after any change that moves prose between this skill and a caller that cites it.

evals.name: the-sequence-runs-summary-walkthrough-ranking-then-gate
evals.prompt: You are executing the settle-and-merge skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). backlog-orchestrator has found its wave settled and invoked you over its eight open PRs. It passed its resolved policy (two repositories opted into auto-merge; auto-request-settle is on) and asked for a ranking, with its cross-branch collisions and held issue set. To save time, a teammate proposes: rank the PRs with plan-merge-order first so merges can start while summarize-wave is still running, then do the summary and the decision walkthrough afterwards for the report. Question: in what order do the steps run, and why?
evals.expected_output: No. Reconcile tracker and remote state first, then summarize-wave, then act on its action points, then request the settle-outstanding-decisions walkthrough (while auto-request-settle is on), then plan-merge-order with the rulings translated into action points, then the gate and the merges, then surface the summary, the walkthrough's report and the ranking. The summary comes before the ranking because an action point can change whether something should merge at all, and the walkthrough sits between summary and ranking because a ruling changes what the ranking is computed from. Ranking first gives the user an order they may start acting on before an action point or ruling invalidates it.
assertions: The answer rejects ranking or merging before the summary
The answer orders the steps reconcile, summary, action points, walkthrough, ranking, gate, surface
The answer gives a reason for the walkthrough sitting between summary and ranking: a ruling changes what the ranking is computed from

evals.name: the-gate-is-evaluated-only-after-its-inputs-exist
evals.prompt: You are executing the settle-and-merge skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Invoked over a wave of three PRs, all in a repository that opted into auto-merge. Before step 2 runs, PR-2 has green CI on its current head, no conflict, a completed clean review, no recovery ref, is not a draft, and its dependency view is proven. A teammate says the gate plainly passes for PR-2 already, so merge it now and run the summary afterwards. Question: may PR-2 merge now?
evals.expected_output: No. The gate is evaluated at step 6, after the summary, the walkthrough and the ranking. Its DECISION and MERGE_RISK inputs do not exist until summarize-wave produces them, so an evaluation before the summary is a guess wearing the gate's name. The outstanding-item test is also wave-wide: a DECISION raised about PR-1 or PR-3 holds PR-2 too, and an unruled DECISION is outstanding. PR-2 waits for step 6.
assertions: The answer refuses to merge PR-2 before the summary runs
The answer says the gate's DECISION/MERGE_RISK inputs do not exist before summarize-wave produces them
The answer notes the outstanding-item test covers the whole wave, not only PR-2

evals.name: publish-then-merge-waits-for-a-later-pass
evals.prompt: You are executing the settle-and-merge skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). At step 6 the gate passes for PR-4, which is still a draft nobody has ever marked ready. Its repository opted into auto-merge, the caller passed no publish rule of its own, and the run has already observed on an earlier PR in this repository that publishing a draft starts an automated review round. Question: what happens to PR-4 in this pass, and when may it merge?
evals.expected_output: It is published, not skipped: publishing is part of the merge path, so a draft whose gate opens is published by the act of merging it. Because publishing is observed to trigger in this repository, publishing un-settles the wave for that PR: the clean-review and green-CI evidence the gate just accepted describes the PR one moment before it changed. It does not merge in this pass and the merge is not awaited inline. It merges on a later delivered pass, once the review round the publish triggered has completed clean; if that re-review finds something, the PR is not clean and returns to ordinary repair as a ready PR.
assertions: The answer publishes PR-4 rather than skipping it for being a draft
The answer refuses to merge in the same pass on pre-publish evidence
The answer refuses an inline wait and defers the merge to a later pass on post-publish evidence

evals.name: a-single-pr-invocation-skips-the-ranking
evals.prompt: You are executing the settle-and-merge skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). implement-issue invoked you over its one PR after its issue reached a terminal state. Its repository opted into auto-merge. It passed: ranking - `caller translates` (it runs its own ruling translation over the rulings you hand back and returns translated action points); dependency view - proven, from its worker's completeness report; freshness checks - none apply; publish rule - `hand back`. summarize-wave returned one DECISION about this PR, and the walkthrough recorded the owner's ruling to hold the PR until a partner team signs off. CI is green, the review is clean and nothing else is outstanding. You hand the ruling back and the caller returns one translated action point: the gate is held for this PR, as a MERGE_RISK would hold it. Question: do you invoke plan-merge-order before evaluating the gate, and does the PR merge?
evals.expected_output: No, and no. The caller passed ranking: `caller translates`, so step 5 ranks nothing — one PR has no ordering to rank. At step 5 this skill hands the walkthrough's ruling to the caller and takes back its translated action points; it does not perform that translation itself. The returned action point holds the gate exactly as a MERGE_RISK would, so at step 6 the PR does not merge and is reported held by it. The wave-wide outstanding-item clause reads as this one PR's own items.
assertions: The answer does not invoke plan-merge-order, because the caller passed `caller translates`
The answer takes the caller's translated action point back at step 5, rather than translating the ruling itself, and applies it before the gate
The answer holds the gate on the returned action point, so the PR does not merge
The answer reads the wave-wide outstanding-item clause as this PR's own items

evals.name: an-absent-input-takes-its-default-not-the-callers-identity
evals.prompt: You are executing the settle-and-merge skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). A new orchestrator invokes you over its one PR. It passes the PR set and scope, its findings, its posting-identity map, and resolved policy (the repository opted into auto-merge), and a dependency view proven complete. It passes nothing about ranking, freshness checks, a publish rule or un-settling. Since the PR has been reviewed clean against a base that has since moved by two merges, a teammate says: it is a single-PR run like implement-issue's, so skip the ranking and the stale-green re-check the way implement-issue does. Question: which of the settle steps and gate-time checks run?
evals.expected_output: Not as the teammate says. An absent input takes its stated default, never a value inferred from which skill the caller resembles. With no ranking input, step 5 runs: a caller that does not rank must pass its own ruling translation, and without one an untranslated ruling would read as clean at the gate. With no freshness input, the stale-green re-check and the tool-bump rule apply (absent is not 'none apply'); the base has moved, so the existing green is stale and does not discharge the CI condition until re-established as the repository's CI configuration requires. No integration result was passed, so there is none to compare, and the report says so. With no publish rule, the three-state rule governs any publish; with no un-settle rule, an un-settling step returns to the caller with the finding, having ranked and merged nothing.
assertions: The answer runs step 5 because no ranking input (and no ruling translation) was passed
The answer applies the stale-green re-check because the freshness input was absent, and treats the green as stale since the base moved
The answer does not infer any input from the caller resembling implement-issue

evals.name: green-is-every-required-check-concluded-on-the-head

assertions: the answer does not treat PR-4 as green with e2e missing
the answer does not treat PR-5's empty rollup as green
the answer enumerates the required checks rather than gating on those it happened to read

evals.name: the-closing-output-lists-unposted-held-replies
evals.prompt: You are executing the settle-and-merge skill (read its SKILL.md, and NOTES.md if present, from the skill directory you were given). Scenario: a run settles on a scheduled wake with nobody present, so the walkthrough declines. The caller passed two approval-pending reply items, each a thread a person is in with its fix pushed and its one-line held reply. Questions: (a) does the closing output mention them, and with what? (b) can the owner recover them later by running settle-outstanding-decisions?
evals.expected_output: (a) Yes: it lists every held reply not yet posted — thread URL, fix SHA and the one-line text — separately from the decisions, so the owner can post it themselves. It also lists each fix pushed on a thread a person is in that also asks a question as 'fix pushed — thread left for you (it also asks a question)'. (b) No. A held reply's text is run state and is dropped when the run ends; no later walkthrough recovers it, and the closing output must not say otherwise. The threads stay open with their fixes pushed. A later run that re-dispatches such a thread finds the change already on the head and composes a fresh held reply rather than fixing it again.
assertions: the closing output lists each unposted held reply with its thread URL, fix SHA and text
the answer says a later settle-outstanding-decisions run cannot recover the held text
the answer says a later re-dispatch finds the change on the head and composes a fresh held reply
the answer does not claim the walkthrough is idempotent over held replies

evals.name: minimize-ci-runs-no-overlap-merges-on-the-existing-green

assertions: the answer finds overlap on src/y.ts
